subject: history
topic_display: Edexcel: Civil Rights & Race in USA 1850-2009
title: Brown to Obama: Civil Rights Movement and After
welcome_lead: From Brown v Board to the election of Barack Obama.
meta_desc: Edexcel A-Level adventure on Brown 1954, MLK, the Voting Rights Act 1965 and Obama's 2008 victory.
final_note: You can evaluate civil rights gains and persistent inequalities by 2009.

concepts.def: Unanimous Supreme Court ruling on 17 May 1954 that segregated public schools violated the 14th Amendment.
1 December 1955-20 December 1956 protest after Rosa Parks's arrest; ended in desegregation of buses (Browder v Gayle).
Federal law signed 2 July 1964 banning discrimination in employment and public accommodations.
Signed 6 August 1965; banned literacy tests and authorised federal supervision of registration.
Movement from 1966 emphasising self-determination, associated with Stokely Carmichael, SNCC and the Black Panthers (1966).
Elected 4 November 2008 as the first African American president of the United States; inaugurated 20 January 2009.

walkthroughs.body_html: Brown (1954) and the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-56) launched the modern movement. The Little Rock Nine (1957) forced Eisenhower to send the 101st Airborne. Greensboro sit-ins (1960) created SNCC; the Freedom Rides (1961) confronted interstate segregation. The Birmingham campaign (April-May 1963), the March on Washington (28 August 1963) and Selma (March 1965) produced the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts.

The Watts Riots (August 1965) and Detroit (1967) exposed Northern racism. The Black Power turn followed; the Black Panther Party (Oakland, October 1966) combined armed self-defence with social programmes. Martin Luther King Jr was assassinated on 4 April 1968 in Memphis; the Fair Housing Act (1968) followed. The Kerner Commission (1968) blamed 'white racism' for urban unrest.

Busing (Swann, 1971) and affirmative action (Bakke, 1978) provoked backlash; Reagan-era cuts hit civil rights enforcement. Jesse Jackson ran in 1984 and 1988. The 1991 Civil Rights Act strengthened employment law. The Los Angeles riots (April-May 1992) followed the Rodney King verdict. Barack Obama won the presidency on 4 November 2008, inaugurated on 20 January 2009, yet wealth and incarceration gaps persisted.
